# Roadmap

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask devlog roadmap` from CATALOG.md. Do not edit by hand. -->

What gets built, in which order. This is planned work, not a claim that
anything works: what is built and tested is in
[`features.toml`](../../features.toml). Each entry, its dependencies and its
gate are in [CATALOG.md](CATALOG.md); CI fails when this page and the catalog
differ. W1 onwards count from the mainnet launch date.

Size: S is up to a few days, M one to three weeks, L longer.

## W0 (12 entries)

Now, before genesis. Non-consensus work only; the frozen node binary is not touched.

**A. Core user apps**

- `hub-launch` (S): Open Wallet and Chat from the Hub through an OS link scheme (ADR-083 decision 4). **Built on `feat/hub-launch`; installed-build registration not yet run**
- `address-text-everywhere` (S): Bech32m `maya1…` in the wallet GUI, explorer, pool, chat and docs (ADR-081 leftovers)
- `signed-installers` (M): Signed installers for Windows, Linux and Android for every app, with auto-update

**D. Builders and operators**

- `finality-latency-bench` (S): Per-transaction submit-to-finalized latency, with the mix, hardware and command stated; closes the measured-finality gap ([COMPETITORS.md](COMPETITORS.md) section 4)

**J. Trust you can verify (research 2026-11-10)**

- `rebuilder-attestations`: A release is trusted because outsiders rebuilt it, not because CI says so
- `claims-ledger`: Every number on the site and in announcements traces to the run that produced it
- `supply-recompute`: Total supply is a figure anyone recomputes, not one the RPC asserts
- `replay-anyone`: Any block's effects reproducible by anyone with one command

**K. Protection for people (research 2026-11-10)**

- `poison-shield` (S): Fix the Bech32m look-alike check; no copy-from-history; contacts-only autocomplete; look-alike incoming transfers collapsed and labelled

**L. Crypto that outlives us (research 2026-11-10)**

- `algo-health`: Holders see, dated and sourced, how each suite stands
- `hybrid-proofs`: "Two signatures" is only as strong as combiner and parser

**M. Rules nobody can bend (research 2026-11-10)**

- `constitution`: Short list of rules no vote or council can change, each checkable

## W1 (35 entries)

Mainnet to +3 months. User apps and builder tools; no consensus changes.

**A. Core user apps**

- `wallet-v2` (L): Clear signing, smart-account recovery without a paper seed, address book, payment requests. **P0+P1 built** (ADR-086: Bech32m confirm, review wired in, address book, poisoning defenses, payment request v2); P2-P6 not started
- `chat-v2` (L): Group chats, attachments, multi-device
- `chat-pay` (M): Send MAYA inside a chat; the wallet signs (ECOSYSTEM.md section 3)
- `explorer-v2` (M): Graphs, address pages in Bech32m, validator and mining pages, screenshot-diff CI (C10). Built on `feat/explorer-v2`; uptime not shown (RPC has no uptime); explorer baselines pending
- `status-v2` (S): Public network status with a history of incidents and gate progress

**B. Money and commerce**

- `merchant-checkout` (M): Payment links, QR invoices and a webhook for shops

**C. Identity and trust**

- `notary` (S): Timestamp and prove that a document existed (hash only, never the file)

**D. Builders and operators**

- `sdks-1.0` (M): Stable Rust, TypeScript, Python and Go SDKs with versioned releases. **Status:** Rust gateway client `maya2c-sdk` and Go Bech32m address codec built; not published (features.toml `rust-gateway-sdk`)
- `dev-portal` (M): Docs, tutorials, playground and contract templates
- `public-api` (M): Indexer API (REST, later GraphQL) for wallets and dashboards
- `mcp-server` (S): AI assistants can read the chain and draft (never sign) transactions
- `node-in-a-box` (M): One-click validator and node installer with health checks
- `testnet-kit` (S): Faucet, local devnet and attack lab for developers
- `validator-recruitment` (M): Public validator onboarding and operator guide, so the validator count can grow beyond the disclosed launch set
- `independent-audit-program` (L): Scoped external audit of the consensus, crypto and ledger crates, with a public report

**J. Trust you can verify (research 2026-11-10)**

- `release-log-anchor`: A swapped or back-dated release is caught even if GitHub or Rekor is compromised
- `public-invariant-monitor`: Anyone can watch for a conservation break or halt without trusting the foundation's watcher
- `signed-incidents`: Outages and attacks recorded so the foundation cannot quietly edit them later
- `validator-ledger`: Validator behaviour (signing, missed rounds, equivocation, stake concentration) public and derived only from signed consensus data
- `foundation-canary`: Users learn if the foundation is compelled or compromised

**K. Protection for people (research 2026-11-10)**

- `undo-send` (M): Opt-in "undo send": a payment waits N blocks in escrow, the recipient sees it pending, the sender cancels until the stated height
- `payee-check`: Payee confirmation like UK CoP / EU VoP without a central name database: the payee signs a label in the payment request; wallet shows Match / Close match / No match against the label and contacts
- `sim-firewall` (M): Simulate before signing; compare with what the app claimed; block a mismatch until read
- `cooling-off` (S): Large first payment to a new payee waits a short timer, then goes through undo-send; prompt asks bank-style push-fraud questions

**L. Crypto that outlives us (research 2026-11-10)**

- `evidence-records`: Archived history stays verifiable after its signing suite is sunset
- `pq-peer-auth`: Close the documented active-impersonation gap
- `key-age-warnings`: Wallets nudge rotation before a sunset
- `light-sunset-witness`: Light clients and wallets learn upgrades and sunsets without trusting the caller (includes M's schedule-witness)
- `lms-release-signing`: Signed updates stay trustworthy past a curve break

**M. Rules nobody can bend (research 2026-11-10)**

- `mempool-stats`: See that block order is not exploited
- `upgrade-readiness`: Everyone sees before height H whether enough validators run the new binary

**N. Out of the box (research 2026-11-10)**

- `flight-recorder`: After an incident anyone replays the network's decisions and checks the same state roots
- `explain-block`: Anyone reads what a block or tx did, matching what the wallet showed
- `promise-ledger`: Roadmap promises with a due height; misses reported automatically
- `trust-facts`: Public sheet of the chain's trust computed only from evidence on disk, gaps scored as gaps

## W2 (26 entries)

+3 to +6 months. Commerce, identity and operator tools; consensus items only at a written activation height.

**A. Core user apps**

- `wallet-mobile` (L): Android wallet (light client); iOS after the MacBook
- `wallet-extension` (M): Browser extension wallet for web apps
- `notifications` (M): Opt-in alerts (payment received, validator down) without a central server

**B. Money and commerce**

- `pos-terminal` (M): Point of sale on an Android phone: QR request, wait for finality, receipt
- `recurring-payments` (M): Subscriptions and payroll with spending limits
- `escrow` (M): Two-party escrow and milestone payments
- `flash-payments` (L): Instant off-chain payment channels for small, frequent payments
- `exchange-ui` (M): Swap and order-book GUI; must pass the B38 ship gate (`min_out` from a quote, 1% default)
- `treasury-multisig` (L): Multisig and MPC treasury app for teams and DAOs

**C. Identity and trust**

- `identity-app` (L): One `did:maya2c` across every app; verifiable credentials wallet
- `names` (M): Human-readable names for addresses

**D. Builders and operators**

- `validator-console` (M): Validator dashboard: uptime, rewards, slashing risk, alerts
- `pool-dashboard` (M): Pool operators' and miners' web view

**F. Fields (detached apps on the shared identity)**

- `defsec-intel` (M): Shared threat intelligence that defenders can verify

**J. Trust you can verify (research 2026-11-10)**

- `witnessed-checkpoints`: A light client can tell if it is shown a split view

**K. Protection for people (research 2026-11-10)**

- `permission-center` (M): One screen of every live allowance, session key and limit with one-tap revoke; expiry by default; no "unlimited" without typed confirmation
- `scam-registry` (M): Signed scam reports kept off chain; wallets subscribe to curators they choose; accused notified and can appeal; reports expire; warn only, never block
- `intent-descriptors` (M): Plain-language contracts: each VM contract ships a descriptor wallets render (ERC-7730 analogue), attested by deployer and chosen curators

**L. Crypto that outlives us (research 2026-11-10)**

- `quantum-canary`: Public, costly signal that a hardness family is breakable, tied to a pre-agreed response
- `sunset-migration`: When a suite sunsets, funds move to a surviving key without a hard fork or trusting the broken key
- `backup-key-commit`: Survive a family break even if offline
- `level5-hybrid`: Long-held value wants margin beyond category 1–3

**M. Rules nobody can bend (research 2026-11-10)**

- `reserves-proof`: Exchanges and bridges listing MAYA prove they hold what they owe

**N. Out of the box (research 2026-11-10)**

- `bench-rerun`: Performance numbers as a spread of signed re-runs, not a best case
- `exploit-bounty-ledger`: Researchers see a reproduced exploit gets paid without negotiation
- `censorship-monitor`: Measured public evidence of exclusion per proposer

## W3 (22 entries)

+6 to +12 months. The AI network, bridges and the fields.

**A. Core user apps**

- `hardware-wallet` (L): Ledger app for ML-DSA signing

**B. Money and commerce**

- `inheritance` (M): Time-locked recovery to heirs if an owner stops signing
- `btc-bridge-app` (L): BTC in and out with SPV proofs
- `rwa-issuance` (L): Tokenized real-world assets with issuer rules
- `grants-quadratic` (M): Community grants and crowdfunding with quadratic matching
- `shielded-pool-enable` (L): Turn on the shielded pool (private transfers), closing the privacy gap to Monero and Zcash ([COMPETITORS.md](COMPETITORS.md) section 4)

**C. Identity and trust**

- `personhood` (L): Human verification without biometrics stored on chain
- `reputation` (L): Portable reputation for marketplaces and freelancers

**D. Builders and operators**

- `contract-studio` (L): Write, test and formally check WASM contracts
- `succinct-state-proofs` (M): Phone-sized proofs that a Maya2C state or epoch hand-off is final. Phase 0 (M0) is built as a native finality light client in `crates/light-client` (ADR-089): quorum checkpoints and committee handoffs, no proof system. Later phases: phone benchmarks, an off-chain epoch-chain proof, then a committee commitment that needs consensus review

**E. AI-native network (post-mainnet; models never in consensus)**

- `verified-inference` (L): Miners' GPUs run open-weight models and are paid per verified job
- `agent-wallets` (M): AI agents with spending limits and human approval for large payments
- `sentinel-ai` (L): Watchdog AI that proposes and never acts (ADR-077)
- `on-device-assistant` (M): Wallet and chat helpers that run locally; nothing leaves the device by default

**F. Fields (detached apps on the shared identity)**

- `offsec-lab` (M): Authorized-scope testing lab, sandboxed, own-assets only
- `mesh-network` (L): Messaging and payments over mesh and radio where the internet is poor
- `iot-anchor` (M): Device data anchored with proofs (sensors, supply chain)
- `research-records` (M): Timestamped, citable research and open data sets
- `quantum-harbor` (L): Move assets from quantum-vulnerable chains under PQ protection (flagship, memory 2026-10-05)

**M. Rules nobody can bend (research 2026-11-10)**

- `holder-veto`: Stakers and holders can delay or block an upgrade they reject

**N. Out of the box (research 2026-11-10)**

- `ai-receipts`: Every AI answer says which model and input produced it
- `phone-watchers`: Citizens run cheap watchers catching withheld data or bad encoding

## W4 (6 entries)

Later. Needs research, legal work or hardware first.

**E. AI-native network (post-mainnet; models never in consensus)**

- `confidential-ai` (L): Inference on private data with attestation
- `ai-marketplace` (L): Market for models, data sets and jobs

**F. Fields (detached apps on the shared identity)**

- `genetics-vault` (L): Owner-controlled genomic data: consent and an access log, data off chain
- `render-market` (L): GPU rendering and simulation jobs with checkable results
- `civil-defence` (L): Disaster coordination and resilient communications, civil uses only

**K. Protection for people (research 2026-11-10)**

- `mutual-cover` (L): Member-owned cover pool for theft losses with public claims; vault custody reports as evidence
